result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say plainly that completion, satisfaction and a same-day quiz don't show better job performance, and both give the director honest wording. B edges ahead because it names more concrete support metrics with 30/60/90-day checkpoints, points out that there was no pre-course quiz, and gives a ready-to-use script without placeholders. A adds useful ideas, such as auditing real tickets, asking agents and leads where they still get stuck, and checking non-training causes, but its director wording relies on blanks to fill in. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say plainly that completion, satisfaction and quiz scores don't show better job performance, and both give usable wording for the director. B is slightly better: it insists on measuring later on real tickets, warns against inventing a baseline, and says clearly that without a comparison the training's effect can't be separated from other changes. A lists many good metrics but is a bit sprawling, and it suggests a pre-course quiz that can no longer be given to a cohort that has already finished.
